title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES the Dhwaj Stambh Pujan, Dhawaja Pujan and Dhwajarohan ceremony of Simhastha Maha Kumbh at Nashik
subtitle: convergence of countless devotees at Kumbh Melas has served as living proof of India’s cultural and spiritual unity and the continuity of traditions: President Droupadi Murmu
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 OCT 2026 8:41PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu graced the Dhwaj Stambh Pujan, Dhawaja Pujan and Dhwajarohan ceremony of Simhastha Maha Kumbh at Nashik, Maharashtra today (October 31, 2026). She also addressed a public programme on the occasion.
In her address, the President said that the tradition of the Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Simhastha Maha Kumbh is as ancient as it is rich. The Kumbh gatherings held on the banks of the Ganga in Haridwar, at the Triveni Sangam in Prayagraj, on the banks of the Shipra in Ujjain, and on the banks of the Godavari at Nashik, are renowned across the globe. The continuous organization of these gatherings over centuries stands as a testament to the strength of our nation’s historical, cultural, social, and spiritual traditions.
The President said that for centuries, the convergence of countless devotees at these Kumbh Melas has served as living proof of India’s cultural and spiritual unity and the continuity of traditions. These gatherings exemplify faith and social harmony. She expressed confidence that the Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Simhastha Maha Kumbh 2027 will serve as a bridge to connect our ancient heritage with the modern times. She wished that this event be an excellent opportunity to connect our younger generation with India’s magnificent heritage and its core life values.
The President said that today, people across the globe are facing numerous crises due to extreme weather conditions. In our own country, including in regions like Maharashtra, many people, especially our farmers, have been affected by drought. Both the central and state governments are making every effort to ensure that our citizens, particularly our farmers, receive support as they navigate these challenges.
Underlining the importance of cleanliness and awareness about the environment, the President urged citizens to continue making sustained efforts, both individually and collectively, toward environmental conservation. She expressed confidence that during the 'Maha Kumbh' at Nashik, the efforts of the event management, combined with active public participation, will set an exemplary standard for cleanliness and waste management.

title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan attends ‘Sardar Katha’ at Uprashtrapati Bhavan; pays tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on Rashtriya Ekta Diwas
subtitle: Calls upon youth to draw inspiration from Sardar Patel’s ideals of unity, discipline and nation-building; says India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat @2047 must be guided by greater ambition and collective resolve
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 OCT 2026 6:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today attended ‘Sardar Katha’, organised at Uprashtrapati Bhavan, marking the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and Rashtriya Ekta Diwas. The programme featured an inspiring narration by renowned Katha Vachika Dr. Shobhana Radhakrishna, highlighting the life, ideals and extraordinary contributions of Sardar Patel to the nation.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan attended ‘Sardar Katha’ at Uprashtrapati Bhavan today, organised  on the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and Rashtriya Ekta Diwas. The Katha was presented by Dr. Shobhana Radhakrishna, bringing alive the life, ideals and contributions of the Iron Man of India.

Emphasising India's remarkable journey since Independence and its march towards Viksit Bharat @ 2047, the Vice-President called upon the youth to imbibe Sardar Patel’s ideals of unity, courage, discipline and selfless service.

The programme was attended by Lieutenant Governor of Delhi Shri Taranjit Singh Sandhu, and other distinguished guests.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
October 31, 2026
Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President extended his greetings on Rashtriya Ekta Diwas and said that Sardar Patel’s story was not merely that of one of India's greatest leaders, but also the story of India's unity, courage and nation-building.
Recalling Sardar Patel’s monumental contribution to the political integration of India, the Vice-President said that at the time of Independence, the country faced enormous challenges, with Partition creating uncertainty and more than 550 princely states needing to be integrated into the Indian Union. Through his determination, persuasion, administrative ability and statesmanship, Sardar Patel accomplished this historic task and gave shape to the vision of a united India. The nation, he said, would always remain grateful for this extraordinary contribution.
The Vice-President said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the spirit of unity championed by Sardar Patel is being channelled into the national mission of Viksit Bharat @2047. He observed that India's journey from 1947 to the present reflected courage, determination and collective resolve, while the journey towards 2047 must be marked by even greater ambition, aspiration and commitment.
Emphasising the continuing relevance of Sardar Patel's ideals, the Vice-President said that truth, simplicity, courage, discipline and service to the last person were values that the nation needed to uphold. He particularly called upon the youth to draw inspiration from Sardar Patel's life and channel their immense energy, talent and potential towards constructive nation-building activities.
Concluding his address, Shri C.P.Radhakrishnan expressed his appreciation to Dr. Shobhana Radhakrishna and her team for bringing Sardar Patel's life and legacy closer to the audience through the timeless tradition of Katha. “Sardar Patel gave us a united India. It is our duty to keep it united, strong and just. Bharat is One, and shall always remain One!” he said.
The programme was attended by Lieutenant Governor of Delhi Shri Taranjit Singh Sandhu, and other distinguished guests.
Earlier in the day, the Vice-President paid floral tributes to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel at Sardar Patel Chowk in New Delhi and at Uprashtrapati Bhavan.
Paid homage to the Iron Man of India, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, on his birth anniversary, observed as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas at Sardar Patel Chowk in New Delhi.

Sardar Patel’s extraordinary life and legacy stand as an enduring testament to the power of national unity, unwavering determination and selfless service.

On this solemn occasion, the nation gratefully remembers his monumental contribution to nation-building and pays heartfelt homage to the great visionary whose legacy continues to guide India’s journey towards unity and progress.

Prepare Civil Services for the India of 2047; Reorient Administrative Systems to Address Emerging Challenges: Vice-President

date:

content:
The Vice-President of India and President of the Indian Institute of Public Administration (IIPA), Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today addressed the 72nd Annual Meeting of the General Body of the Indian Institute of Public Administration in New Delhi. Union Minister and Chairman of the IIPA Executive Council, Dr. Jitendra Singh; Director General, IIPA, Dr. Surendra Kumar Bagde; members of the General Body and Executive Council; faculty members; representatives of Regional and Local Branches; and other dignitaries attended the meeting.
Vice-President of India and President of the Indian Institute of Public Administration (IIPA), Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today addressed the 72nd Annual General Body Meeting of IIPA in New Delhi.

The Vice-President called for citizen-centric governance, better coordination across all levels of administration, a balanced approach to economic growth and environmental sustainability. He urged IIPA to prepare civil servants for the challenges of Viksit Bharat @ 2047.

Union Minister and Chairman of the IIPA Executive Council, Dr. Jitendra Singh, Director General, IIPA, Dr. Surendra Kumar Bagde, members of the General Body and Executive Council, faculty members, representatives of Regional and Local Branches, officers and staff of the Institute and other distinguished guests attended the meeting.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
October 31, 2026
Highlighting the significance of the occasion coinciding with Rashtriya Ekta Diwas and the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the Vice-President paid tribute to the Iron Man of India, describing him as the architect of India’s political integration, who united hundreds of princely states into one nation.
The Vice-President appreciated the significant institutional reforms undertaken by IIPA during 2026, including the redesigned 52nd Advanced Professional Programme, the structured Internship Programme and the engagement of officers from the Central Civil Services and Central Civil Accounts Service. He observed that these initiatives had strengthened the Institute’s administrative and financial architecture. He also commended Dr. Jitendra Singh for his guidance and support and appreciated the Director General, faculty and staff for their efforts in advancing IIPA as a premier institution for public administration.
Observing that public administration was at a critical juncture, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that governance today was increasingly expected to be faster, citizen-centric, technology-enabled, data-driven and outcome-oriented. The Vice-President emphasised that good governance should not be measured merely by economic growth but also by its impact on people's happiness, living standards and overall well-being.
Highlighting India's progress in poverty reduction, the Vice-President noted that, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi over the past 12 years, more than 25 crore people had been brought out of poverty. He described this as a significant achievement reflecting the impact of sustained efforts towards inclusive development and improved living standards. He reiterated that the ultimate objective of governance must be to ensure that economic progress translates into dignity, security and better opportunities for every citizen.
The Vice-President stressed that effective public administration required seamless coordination among the Central Government, State Governments and district-level administration. He said that governance could deliver meaningful results only when different levels of administration worked together with a shared vision and common purpose.
The Vice-President emphasised the need for a balanced and pragmatic approach towards environmental protection and economic development.  He stressed that natural resources must be utilised judiciously for the betterment of people while ensuring environmental sustainability.
The Vice-President urged IIPA to focus its work on the changing role of civil services in realising the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047. He observed that India’s administrative structures had largely evolved when the country was predominantly rural and agriculture was the principal source of livelihood. However, with the country undergoing rapid transformation, administrative systems must also be reoriented to address emerging realities. He urged IIPA to take the lead in this important endeavour and prepare the next generation of civil servants.
Concluding his address, the Vice-President observed that IIPA had a significant responsibility in India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat @ 2047. He called upon IIPA and its members to work collectively towards ensuring that India’s governance framework remained responsive, inclusive, ethical and future-ready.
During the occasion, the Vice-President also conferred the Paul H. Appleby Award, the Dr. Rajendra Prasad Award for Academic Excellence, and the Best IIPA Branches Awards at the 72nd Annual General Body Meeting, recognising distinguished contributions to the Indian Institute of Public Administration and the field of public administration.

title: English rendering of PM’s speech at the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas programme in Kevadia, Gujarat
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 OCT 2026 9:34PM by PIB Delhi
content:
I will say, “Sardar Patel,” and all of you respond, “Immortal forever, immortal forever.”
Sardar Patel – Immortal forever, immortal forever.
Sardar Patel – Immortal forever, immortal forever.
Sardar Patel – Immortal forever, immortal forever.
My dear countrymen,
Today’s event is somewhat different. Until now, we have always held this programme on Unity Day in the morning. This time, there has been a slight change. We have all gathered in the evening. In the morning, lakhs and lakhs of citizens participated in the Run for Unity with a pledge of national unity. We saw the enthusiasm of the people in the Run for Unity. Yesterday evening, I witnessed magnificent presentations at the Bharat Parv Pavilion. And now, on this national occasion, we are present at the feet of Sardar Patel.
Friends,
This is the world’s tallest statue, the Statue of Unity. The participation of the entire nation in its construction, the unique aura of this place, and the extraordinary energy and inspiration of Unity Day fill one’s heart with pride and gratitude upon coming here. Pride in being a citizen of this great nation, and gratitude towards Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who united more than 550 princely states after Independence. With an iron resolve, he bound this nation together in the thread of unity.
Friends,
Freedom is essential for any nation. When a nation is free, it determines its own future. But freedom receives the right direction through a republic. A republic shows us the path of taking decisions within the framework of the Constitution. The Constitution keeps us accountable to the people. And unity gives us the strength to move forward as one nation. That is why in our country, Independence Day, Republic Day, and Unity Day are all celebrated with great enthusiasm as national festivals.
Friends,
Once again today, in Ekta Nagar, we have witnessed the grand vision of India’s unity. This year’s National Unity Parade has also been extraordinary. This parade is dedicated to the courage and bravery of our police and security forces. Through the tableaux, the nation’s heritage and aspirations have been presented before the country. Therefore, Unity Day is no longer limited merely to official events. Through public participation, it has become a celebration of national pride. On this occasion, I extend my greetings to all countrymen on National Unity Day. I bow with deep reverence at the feet of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
Friends,
Sardar Patel is that great personality in India’s history without whom it is difficult even to imagine present-day India. It was Sardar Patel who shaped the India we know today. Even after Partition, the person who kept India secure from the Himalayas to the Indian Ocean was Sardar Patel.
Friends,
Sardar Patel was able to do this because he understood the character and consciousness of India. He knew that India’s diversity was not its weakness. He knew that India’s diversity was, in fact, the true foundation of its unity. For thousands of years, we have lived in this manner. Through this very strength, we touched the heights of progress and prosperity.
Friends,
Sardar Patel once again laid the foundation of that India. He did not merely shape the geography of the nation; he also bound the country together through emotional unity. Through the reconstruction of the Somnath Temple in Gujarat, he also initiated the cultural renaissance of the nation.
Friends,
This year marks the 75th anniversary of that great work as well. Just as the flag of the Somnath Temple has been flying with pride for a thousand years despite the repeated destruction attempted by aggressors, that same spirit of self-respect inspired us to celebrate the Somnath Swabhiman Parva. And this year, the nation is celebrating that occasion with equal enthusiasm.
My dear countrymen,
Today, these great ceremonies of national unity, India’s rising stature on the global stage, the rapid pace of our economic progress, and the revival of our sacred centres from Kashi Vishwanath to the Ram Temple, all point to the direction in which India is moving. It is a path shown to us by Sardar Patel. And for this, the nation will remain indebted to him forever.
Friends,
Last year, we celebrated the 150th birth anniversary of Sardar Patel. For two years, programmes and celebrations were organised across the country. We took major resolutions for the nation and pledged to fulfil them. And today, as we celebrate his 151st birth anniversary, we can say with satisfaction that the nation has fulfilled those resolutions within a very short period of time. In these two years, the country has achieved several unprecedented accomplishments.
Friends,
On the occasion of Sardar Patel’s 150th birth anniversary, standing here at his feet, I had said, “Until the country is completely free from Naxalism and Maoist terror, we will not rest.” And exactly one year later, as we stand here today, that national resolve has been fulfilled. Today, the backbone of Naxalism has been broken in the country. In 2015, 126 districts of the country were affected by Left-wing extremism. By March 2026, not a single district remained in the country that was still affected by Naxalism. These districts, which suffered for decades from violence and bloodshed, are now becoming part of the mainstream of development. Today, roads are expanding in these areas. Mobile networks are reaching people. Educational and healthcare facilities are increasing. Youth who once faced uncertainty now have new opportunities for education, employment, and progress.
Friends,
This time, at this Unity Day celebration, families from Naxal-affected regions have joined us here as special guests. I welcome all of them and wish them a bright future. Today, I also pay my respects to all those brave security personnel who made the supreme sacrifice to establish peace in these regions of the country.
Friends,
Today, India is more secure than before. Today, India is more determined than before. And one major reason for this is the increased confidence of our citizens. Confidence comes from achievements. Confidence comes from the sensitivity of the government and the system. Today, I would certainly like to speak about one such major national achievement.
Friends,
Talks of removing poverty in India have been going on since Independence. Votes were sought in the name of eradicating poverty. But we all know what the actual condition of poverty in the country was. Those who raised the slogan of removing poverty themselves kept becoming richer. Change in circumstances began to come in recent years. Just a few days ago, a World Bank report was released. The report states that in the ten to twelve years before 2024, fifty crore Indians defeated poverty. That means where earlier 27 out of every 100 people, more than one-fourth of the population, were trapped in extreme poverty, today that number has fallen to less than 3 out of every 100 people.
Friends,
The entire world is acknowledging that this is a major achievement. But how did this happen? It happened because for the past twelve years, the country has prioritised the welfare and empowerment of the poor. During these twelve years, the nation received a leak-proof system. Through DBT, every rupee sent from Delhi reached the poor. Free ration and free healthcare helped poor families save money. Crores of permanent houses, crores of toilets, and smoke-free kitchens made life easier for the poor. Crores of people received the protection of insurance, which became a source of support during times of crisis. Before 2014, even 25 crore people in the country did not have any social security coverage. Today, nearly 100 crore people in the country have been connected to a social security safety net.
Friends,
Today, when the entire nation is remembering and paying tribute to Sardar Saheb, his soul must surely be blessing us. Through such efforts, we will eliminate poverty from the country and build a Developed India.
Friends,
National unity guarantees a nation's stability and success. And in times of global instability such as these, the importance of unity has increased even more. You all know that today the world is burning in the fires of unrest. This is among the most difficult periods of the past several decades. Wars are taking place between many countries around the world. Major economies are struggling with challenges. The crisis of resources continues to grow. Global supply chains are becoming fragmented. At such a time, India's unity, the unity of all Indians, is our greatest strength. Because it is this unity that will help us overcome every storm.
Brothers and sisters,
In recent months, we have seen the world struggling with an energy crisis. In some countries, limits were even imposed on the purchase of petrol and diesel. It was being said that India would face the biggest crisis because it has such a large population and does not produce sufficient petroleum. Amid these concerns, anti-India forces also became active.
But friends,
This is India's strength. We did not allow the impact of this global energy crisis to fall upon our citizens. This is certainly a diplomatic and strategic success for the country, but the unity and solidarity of our people played an equally important role. While the nation was looking for solutions to external challenges, certain forces within the country were busy spreading lies and rumours in an attempt to create instability. But the people of India stood shoulder to shoulder with the nation. This is the greatest strength of this country. This is the strongest foundation of our confidence.
Friends,
When great leaders such as Sardar Patel and Babasaheb Ambedkar created the Constitution of India, they established the system of a ruling side and an opposition side. They also explained the importance of this arrangement. In a democracy, the responsibility of the opposition is to oppose government policies. But unfortunately, in today's India, the opposition has abandoned its duty and has transformed itself from an opposition into an obstruction. In its frustration and despair, it has begun placing obstacles in the path of the country's development. This is not opposition; this is obstruction. They have made it the basis of their politics. They are engaged in tearing apart the dignity and spirit of the Constitution.
Friends,
These forces are continuously engaged in conspiracies to divide the nation. Attempts are being made to divide and pit against one another the children of Mother India. Due to more than a decade of frustration and disappointment, these people have now come out in the open. We must identify who is secretly meeting whom abroad, which anti-India forces are supporting whom, and who is speaking the language of India's enemies. We must recognise these patterns. We must unite and confront them. Especially the way social media is being used as a weapon, the way rumours are being spread, and the efforts being made to damage India's image, all citizens must come together to deal with these challenges. We have ended Naxalism in remote regions. But the threat of intellectual Naxalism has not yet disappeared from the country. The nation must always remain vigilant against these intellectual Naxals.
Friends,
No matter how difficult the circumstances may be, we must not allow this grand mission of national unity and this journey towards a strong and capable India to stop. We must now work towards the next major goals. We must secure the nation's borders completely. We must stop infiltration and demographic changes caused by it. We must also move forward towards a Secular Civil Code.
Friends,
Whenever a nation takes great resolutions, whenever it takes major decisions, obstacles will arise, difficulties will appear, and storms will have to be faced. But India is no longer going to stop. The mantra of "Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat" and the goal of a Developed India have now become India's unwavering resolve. We will push ourselves to the limits of hard work. We will confront every storm with determination. But our eyes will remain fixed on one objective alone: building a strong, capable, and developed India by 2047, when the nation completes 100 years of independence. This passion must be present in every effort we make and in every breath we take. This idea must beat with every heartbeat in our hearts. With this resolve, I once again extend my heartfelt greetings to all of you on National Unity Day.
Bharat Mata Ki Jai!
Bharat Mata Ki Jai!
Bharat Mata Ki Jai!
Vande Mataram.
Vande Mataram.
Vande Mataram.
Thank you very much.

date:

content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today participated in the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations marking the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel in Ekta Nagar, Gujarat. Addressing the gathering, the Prime Minister highlighted the shift from the traditional morning schedule to an evening ceremony, recalling the magnificent showcase at the Bharat Parv Pavilion the previous evening and the massive turnout of lakhs of citizens resolved to uphold unity during the morning's Run for Unity.
Pointing to the collective nationwide participation in building the world's tallest statue, the Statue of Unity, alongside the unique aura of the venue and the inspiring energy of Unity Day, the Prime Minister stated that visiting the monument fills the heart with pride in being an Indian citizen and deep gratitude toward Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. “After independence, he united more than 550 princely states and wove this nation into the thread of unity with iron determination,” affirmed PM Modi.
Explaining that while independence empowers a nation to shape its own destiny and a republic guides decisions within constitutional bounds to ensure public accountability, the Prime Minister emphasized that unity provides the vital strength to advance together as one nation. “Therefore, in our country now, Independence Day, Republic Day, and Unity Day, all three national festivals are celebrated with full enthusiasm,” noted Shri Modi.
Highlighting the grand spectacle of national unity at Ekta Nagar through this year's National Unity Parade dedicated to the valor of police and security forces and tableaus showcasing India's heritage and aspirations, the Prime Minister observed that Unity Day has evolved beyond mere formal events into a celebration of public pride driven by public participation. “On this occasion, I congratulate all countrymen on National Unity Day, and I bow with reverence at the feet of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel,” remarked PM Modi.
Describing Sardar Patel as a towering historical figure without whom modern India cannot be imagined, the Prime Minister credited him with shaping the nation's present geographical and political form. “Even after Partition, the one who kept India safe from the Himalayas to the Indian Ocean was Sardar Patel himself,” asserted Shri Modi.
Stating that Sardar Patel succeeded because he deeply understood India's character and consciousness, the Prime Minister explained that the leader recognized diversity not as a hurdle, but as the true foundation of national unity that has sustained Indian civilization for millennia. “With this very strength, we have touched the peaks of progress and prosperity,” observed PM Modi.
Emphasizing that Sardar Patel laid the foundation of modern India by uniting the country both geographically and emotionally, the Prime Minister highlighted his pivotal role in initiating the nation's cultural resurgence. “Through the reconstruction of the Somnath Temple in Gujarat, he also initiated the cultural resurgence of the nation,” noted Shri Modi.
Noting that this year marks the 75th anniversary of the Somnath Temple's reconstruction, the Prime Minister stated that the temple flag flying proudly for a thousand years in defiance of tyrants inspired the ongoing Somnath Swabhiman Parv across the country. “And this year the country is celebrating this festival too with the same enthusiasm,” observed PM Modi.
Connecting the grand ceremonies of national unity, India's rising global stature, rapid economic growth, and the cultural revival spanning from Kashi Vishwanath to the Ram Temple, the Prime Minister stated that the nation is advancing along the very path envisioned by Sardar Patel. “And for this, this country will always remain indebted to him,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Recalling the two-year nationwide celebrations marking Sardar Patel's 150th birth anniversary during which the country took major pledges, the Prime Minister expressed satisfaction on his 151st birth anniversary that those resolutions have been fulfilled within a remarkably short span. “In these two years, the country has achieved several unprecedented milestones,” noted PM Modi.
Reminding the nation of his solemn vow made at Sardar Patel's feet during the 150th birth anniversary not to rest until Naxalism and Maoist terror were completely eradicated, the Prime Minister declared that the back of Left-Wing Extremism has been broken within a year, reducing the number of Naxal-affected districts from 126 in 2015 to zero by March 2026. He highlighted that regions scarred by decades of bloodshed are now joining the developmental mainstream with expanding roads, mobile networks, schools, and healthcare facilities. “For the youth who once faced uncertainty, new opportunities for education, employment, and moving forward are opening up,” asserted Shri Modi.
Welcoming families from formerly Naxal-affected regions attending the Unity Day celebrations as special guests and wishing them a bright future, the Prime Minister paid homage to the security personnel who laid down their lives for peace. “Today I also bow to all those brave soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice to establish peace in these regions of the country,” affirmed PM Modi.
Observing that India today is safer and more resolute due to heightened public confidence born from tangible national accomplishments and a sensitive administration, the Prime Minister highlighted the historic milestone achieved in poverty alleviation after decades of hollow post-independence slogans where those chanting Garibi Hatao only enriched themselves. He cited a recent World Bank report revealing that 50 crore Indians overcame poverty in the 10 to 12 years prior to 2024. “Meaning, where earlier 27 out of 100 people were in the grip of extreme poverty, today this number has remained less than 3,” noted Shri Modi.
Explaining that this globally acclaimed feat was achieved by prioritizing poor welfare and empowerment over the past 12 years through leakage-free Direct Benefit Transfers, free ration, free healthcare, crores of pucca homes, toilets, smoke-free kitchens, and wide insurance coverage, the Prime Minister pointed out that social security coverage has expanded from under 25 crore people before 2014 to nearly 100 crore citizens today. Invoking Sardar Patel's blessings as the nation pays tribute to him, he reiterated the resolve to completely eradicate poverty. “With such efforts alone, we will remove poverty in the country and make the country a Viksit Bharat,” asserted PM Modi.
Emphasizing that national unity guarantees stability and success during the most turbulent global era in decades marked by wars, economic distress, resource crunches, and fractured supply chains, the Prime Minister stated that the solidarity of Indians remains the country's greatest pillar of strength to weather every global storm. Pointing to the recent international energy crisis that forced fuel rationing in several nations and sparked predictions of severe distress for populous, oil-importing India amid the activation of anti-India forces, he credited both diplomatic agility and public solidarity for shielding citizens from the shock.
Warning against divisive forces that have come out in the open after more than a decade of political frustration to plot conspiracies, pit citizens against one another, and weaponize social media to spread rumors and tarnish India's image, the Prime Minister urged citizens to recognize the patterns of secret foreign meetings, external backing from anti-India elements, and rhetoric echoing the nation's enemies. “We have ended Naxalism in remote areas, but the danger of ideological extremists has not yet passed from over the country, and the country has to remain ever vigilant against such entities,” cautioned Shri Modi.
Stressing that the grand mission of national unity and the journey toward a strong and capable India must continue unabated regardless of difficulties, the Prime Minister outlined the next major national priorities of completely securing India's borders, halting infiltration and demographic changes, and advancing toward a Secular Civil Code. Acknowledging that major resolutions and bold decisions will inevitably face roadblocks and storms, he declared that the nation will not be deterred from the unwavering resolves of Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat and a Viksit Bharat, working tirelessly with every breath and heartbeat toward the 2047 goal before concluding with festive greetings and chants of Bharat Mata Ki Jai. “We will reach the pinnacle of hard work, we will firmly confront tempests, but our vision will remain on a single goal, the making of a strong and capable India by 2047!” asserted PM Modi.

subtitle:
SARDAR VALLABHBHAI PATEL'S VISION, FIRM RESOLVE AND ORGANISATIONAL SKILLS REMAIN AN ENDURING INSPIRATION FOR NATION-BUILDING: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

LOK SABHA SPEAKER PAYS TRIBUTES TO SARDAR VALLABHBHAI PATEL IN CENTRAL HALL OF SAMVIDHAN SADAN

MINISTERS, MEMBERS OF PARLIAMENT AND OTHER DIGNITARIES ALSO PAY TRIBUTES TO SARDAR VALLABHBHAI PATEL IN CENTRAL HALL

CHILDREN FROM VARIOUS COLLEGES AND SCHOOLS ALSO PAY TRIBUTES TO SARDAR VALLABHBHAI PATEL
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 OCT 2026 8:48PM by PIB Delhi
content:
New Delhi; 31 October, 2026
: Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla paid floral tributes at the portrait of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan on his birth anniversary today.
Union Minister of Defence Shri Rajnath Singh; Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare and Chemicals and Fertilizers Shri J. P. Nadda; Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs and Minority Affairs Shri Kiren Rijiju; Leader of Opposition in Rajya Sabha Shri Mallikarjun Kharge; Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri Harivansh; Members of Parliament, including Shri Nitin Nabin and Smt. Sonia Gandhi; former Members and other dignitaries also paid floral tributes at the portrait of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on the occasion.
Secretary General, Lok Sabha, Shri Utpal Kumar Singh and Secretary General, Rajya Sabha, Shri P. C. Mody, along with senior officers of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha Secretariats, also joined the dignitaries in paying tributes to Sardar Patel.
On this occasion, addressing young students and participants from different colleges and schools, Shri Birla called upon the youth to draw inspiration from the life and ideals of the Iron Man, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, and to dedicate their abilities, innovation and collective efforts to strengthening India's national unity and integrity and building a developed nation.
Shri Birla said that the life of Sardar Patel, the architect of modern India's national unity, exemplified firm resolve, exceptional organisational skills, farsightedness and decisive leadership. Recalling Sardar Patel's remarkable contribution to national integration, he observed that despite numerous challenges and adverse circumstances following Independence, his unwavering commitment to the nation enabled him to integrate around 560 princely states into the Indian Union. The unity and integrity of India as we see it today owes an immeasurable debt to his leadership and vision. He also highlighted Sardar Patel's ability to engage in dialogue, take firm decisions when required and carry everyone along in pursuit of a common national objective.
Referring to the students assembled in the Central Hall, Shri Birla appreciated their thoughtfulness, self-confidence, decision-making abilities and spirit of innovation. He observed that the diversity of opinions and perspectives expressed by young people from different parts of the country reflected the inherent strength of India's democracy. While cultures, languages, political systems and viewpoints may differ, the commitment to national unity and the larger interests of the country must remain common and paramount. Lok Sabha Speaker noted that Samvidhan Sadan holds a special place in India's national journey, having witnessed the freedom struggle and the making of the Constitution. It has also been a venue for deliberations and decisions concerning the country's economic and social development and the making of a new India. He expressed confidence that young people, carrying the ideas, perspectives and inspiration gained from this historic institution, would contribute meaningfully to the vision of a developed India.
Emphasising the responsibility of the younger generation in nation-building, Shri Birla said that while great personalities had secured Independence and laid the foundations of a new India through their sacrifices and contributions, it was now the responsibility of the youth to take the nation forward. With the strength of science and technology, abundant knowledge, resources, self-confidence and innovative capabilities, India's young generation has immense opportunities to make meaningful contributions across diverse fields. Lok Sabha Speaker urged young people to channel their creativity, spirituality, scientific temper and technological capabilities towards the service of the nation. He stressed that national interest must remain the foremost priority for young people working in every sphere and that the collective efforts of the country's leadership and youth would be instrumental in realising the vision of an India that leads the world.
Expressing hope that the ideas shared by the young participants would inspire youth across the country with renewed energy, direction, confidence and determination, Shri Birla said that India's younger generation should imbibe the vision, hard work, firm resolve and self-confidence exemplified by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. He expressed confidence that these qualities would enable India to emerge as a transformative global force and contribute solutions to challenges confronting the world.
Earlier in the day, Shri Birla, in his message on X, had stated, "On the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Ji, the Iron Man of India and the recipient of the Bharat Ratna, I pay my heartfelt tributes to the great visionary whose unwavering resolve and exceptional leadership gave a new direction to the unity, integrity and sovereignty of our nation.
From playing a leading role in the freedom struggle to shaping the destiny of independent India, Sardar Patel Ji's contribution to the nation remains unparalleled and unforgettable. As the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of independent India, he successfully addressed one of the most formidable challenges confronting the newly independent nation by playing a decisive role in the integration of more than 562 princely states. His extraordinary leadership and political foresight strengthened the foundations of a united and powerful India.
Sardar Patel Ji's vision extended beyond the attainment of independence; he aspired to build a strong, self-reliant and cohesive nation where diversity would be our strength and national unity our defining identity. The observance of his birth anniversary as National Unity Day reminds us of our collective responsibility towards preserving the unity, integrity and security of our nation. Let us draw inspiration from his ideals and resolve to contribute wholeheartedly towards building a strong, harmonious and developed India."

content:
New Delhi, 31 October 2026
: Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today paid rich tributes to the revered spiritual luminaries Acharya Shri Ram Sharma Ji and Mata Bhagwati Devi Ji at the Shatabdi Samaroh 2026, recalling their invaluable contributions to India's spiritual renaissance, social transformation and nation-building. He observed that the centenary celebration was not merely an occasion to commemorate the past, but a celebration of a creative movement that had transformed countless lives across the country.
Paying homage to Acharya Shri Ram Sharma Ji during his address at the centenary celebration organised by Gayatri Parivar in New Delhi, Shri Birla said that through Akhand Jyoti, he had spread the light of spirituality across the country and inspired people with the ideals of individual development, family development, social development and nation-building. His inspiring resolve, “We will change, and the era will change”, had become a guiding principle for people in India and across the world. Through the Gayatri Mantra and yajna, Acharya Ji connected people with spiritual consciousness and paved the way for inner purity and spiritual awakening.
Recalling his personal association with the Gayatri Parivar, Shri Birla said that he had witnessed the transformative influence of Acharya Ji's spiritual philosophy even in remote villages and hamlets, where it had helped people overcome difficult circumstances, superstition and harmful social practices. The movement had not only brought about a change in people's social lives but had also contributed to their personal growth, character-building and a deeper sense of responsibility towards society and the nation.
Paying his respectful homage to Mata Bhagwati Devi Ji, the Lok Sabha Speaker highlighted her extraordinary life of maternal affection, compassion, penance, dedication and service. He said that her contribution went far beyond spiritual awakening, as she spearheaded a significant movement for social transformation and women's empowerment at a time when women across the country faced numerous social challenges and restrictive practices. He observed that Mata Ji inspired women to pursue education, develop self-confidence and become self-reliant. Her life and teachings demonstrated that the development of a woman's personality within a household lays the foundation for the progress of the entire family and society. Her maternal affection and compassionate guidance transformed the lives of countless women and gave a new impetus to their social and spiritual empowerment. An environment rooted in spiritual awareness and Indian values, he said, played an important role in nurturing positive attitudes, strengthening families and building a progressive society.
Shri Birla appreciated the Gayatri Parivar's sustained efforts to take India's spiritual heritage, cultural wisdom and value-based philosophy to different parts of the world. He noted that the organisation, through its work in several countries, had been advancing the ideals of individual, family and social development in keeping with contemporary needs. He also appreciated the institution's commitment to education rooted in spirituality, culture and Indian values.
Referring to the university established by Acharya Ji, the Lok Sabha Speaker said that its emphasis on spirituality, cultural values and character-building from the early stages of education was commendable.
He expressed appreciation for the institution's initiatives in value-based education, women's awakening and empowerment, and social reform. He also lauded Dr. Chinmaya Pandya for taking India's spiritual traditions and cultural values to the world while simultaneously familiarising people with developments in science and technology. Emphasising the relevance of spirituality in the contemporary world, Shri Birla said that at a time when people in several countries were experiencing stress and depression, the message of inner peace, spiritual strength and a purposeful life had become increasingly significant. The Gayatri Parivar's spiritual centre, he observed, provided people with peace of mind, self-confidence, determination and a sense of direction in life. Shri Birla called upon the Gayatri Pariwar to continue carrying the light of Akhand Jyoti to every village and every section of society. He emphasised that this mission must continue until the life of the last person in society was touched by positive transformation. The ideals of spirituality, religion, culture, character-building and nation-building, he said, must remain central to this endeavour.
Expressing confidence in the continued contribution of the Gayatri Parivar, Shri Birla said that the spiritual energy and consciousness inspired by Acharya Shri Ram Sharma Ji and Mata Bhagwati Devi Ji would continue to illuminate lives and strengthen the foundations of a harmonious, enlightened and developed society.

subtitle: Yoga 365 initiative to encourage daily Yoga practice, collective well-being and social harmony

content:
On the occasion of National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas) 2026, commemorating the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the Ministry of Ayush is promoting the message of ‘Yoga for Unity’, highlighting the role of Yoga in fostering national integration, social harmony and collective well-being.
The initiative, integrated with Yoga 365, aims to encourage citizens to make Yoga an integral part of their daily lives while strengthening the spirit of togetherness and shared responsibility towards health and well-being. The Ministry is encouraging its Yoga and Naturopathy institutions across the country to undertake activities that take the message of Yoga for Unity to communities and promote wider public participation.
Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush and Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare, said, “Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel united the nation through his vision and determination. On National Unity Day, we must carry forward his message of unity through collective action. Yoga brings people together beyond differences of age, region and background, promoting physical and mental well-being. Through Yoga for Unity and Yoga 365, we encourage every citizen to embrace Yoga as a daily practice and contribute towards building a healthier and more united India.”
Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, said, “Yoga offers a simple and accessible means of improving physical and mental well-being while fostering a sense of connection among individuals and communities. Through Yoga for Unity, we aim to strengthen this message and encourage wider community participation in building a culture of health, harmony and collective well-being.”

title: High level CAQM Team reviews Paddy Straw Management Measures reviews in Sangrur, Patiala and Malerkotla of Punjab

content:
A high level Team of Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) comprising Dr. S.D. Attri, Member Technical and Sh. Vijay Kumar, Scientist ‘C’ from CAQM, held a review meeting with Deputy Commissioners, SSPs and officers from PPCB and Agriculture Department of Districts Sangrur, Patiala and Malerkotla and flying squads of CPCB at District Administrative Complex, Sangrur on 31.10.2026. The meeting focused on reviewing preparation and management of paddy straw and control of stubble fires of these districts by the District Administrations. The team visited an Ex-situ paddy stubble utilisation facility, a duplex board/paper making unit at Dhuri Road, Malerkotla, which uses paddy straw as fuel in its boiler of capacity 20 TPH. The representatives of the industry informed that about 17000 MT of paddy straw would be utilised in its boiler furnace on an annual basis.
The team also saw in-situ machinery working in village Ahmadabad of District Malerkotla. Working of super seeder was also shown by Agricultural Department. Further, the team met farmers, who in turn assured that they will not burn paddy straw and manage the same using in-situ machinery. The team reviewed arrangements and measures being undertaken by the District Administrations and concerned departments for effective management of paddy straw and prevention of stubble burning during the ongoing harvesting season.
The CAQM team visited different villages namely Bassiark, Kapial and Jhaneri in Bhawanigarh Tehsil of District Sangrur. Further, at village Gharachon, a hotspot village, ex-situ and and in-situ management of paddy straw were demonstrated. During the visit, the team interacted with farmers of this hotspot village. The CAQM team was also informed about preparedness of the District Administration and the arrangements made for ensuring the availability of Crop Residue Management (CRM) machinery to farmers for in-situ management of paddy straw. Farmers explained the difficulties faced by them regarding utilization of CRM machinery.
The team visited a paddy straw pelletizing manufacturing unit at Village Nadampur, Bhawanigarh. The CAQM officials, accompanied by officers of the Punjab Pollution Control Board (PPCB) and the District Administration, Sangrur obtained first-hand information regarding the utilisation of paddy straw for manufacturing biomass pellets, which are subsequently used as fuel in thermal power plants. The team was apprised that such pellet manufacturing units are playing a significant role in promoting ex-situ management of paddy straw by providing an alternative avenue for its utilisation, thereby helping farmers avoid crop residue burning and contributing towards the prevention of stubble burning incidents.
The CAQM officials asked concerned departments to continue making concerted efforts with close monitoring to ensure effective prevention of stubble burning incidents. title: MoHUA Conducts Participatory Workshop to Chart a Shared Roadmap for Clean Delhi
date:

content:
Department of Capital Development, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) in collaboration with Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban organised a workshop on Planning a Shared Roadmap for Clean Delhi, bringing together sanitation inspectors, supervisors, urban local body officials and key stakeholders to collectively deliberate on practical solutions for making the national capital cleaner, healthier and more liveable. Ms. D. Thara, Secretary, Department of Capital Development, MoHUA, along with senior officials from NDMC, MCD, DDA, and MoHUA, participated in the workshop.
The workshop, “Planning a Shared Roadmap for Clean Delhi,” was envisioned to bring stakeholders together to understand these challenges and co-create practical solutions. For the first time, functionaries from the top to the lowest level, came together on a common platform to deliberate on critical issues and chart a collective path towards a cleaner Delhi.
Sanitation staff, being at the forefront of service delivery, are the ones who are able to share first-hand insights into everyday operational challenges, enabling stakeholders to brainstorm and ideate practical, on-ground solutions alongside policy interventions. An online digital poll was conducted among the participants to identify key challenges affecting cleanliness in Delhi and gather insights from stakeholders working at the grassroots level. The exercise provided valuable feedback on operational gaps, citizen behaviour, service delivery challenges and opportunities for improvement.
As a mark of appreciation for their exemplary contribution towards urban sanitation, the invited Sanitary Inspectors and Supervisors were felicitated for their dedicated efforts in maintaining cleanliness across the city. The workshop commenced with an inspiring motivational address by the distinguished spiritual leader BK Hussain from Brahma Kumaris.
A major highlight of the workshop was an extensive interactive discussion centred around ten critical questions aimed at developing a collective roadmap for a Clean Delhi. The deliberations focused on some of the most pressing urban sanitation challenges, including the reasons Delhi continues to struggle with visible cleanliness despite significant investments and efforts; strategies for transitioning towards a bin-less city through more efficient and frequent door-to-door waste collection; recurring Garbage Vulnerable Points (GVPs) and measures to prevent littering and waste from entering water bodies; and ensuring that public toilets remain clean, safe and functional throughout the day. The discussions also explored ways to improve citizen grievance redressal systems. Best practices were highlighted as success stories while also sharing photographs & incidents requiring focussed efforts and targeted interventions.
The deliberations brought together perspectives from sanitation workers, inspectors, supervisors, urban local body representatives and policymakers, fostering a collaborative dialogue on strengthening urban sanitation systems and enhancing accountability for improving visible cleanliness in Delhi.
Addressing the gathering, Ms. D. Thara, Secretary, DoCD, MoHUA, congratulated the Sanitary Inspectors and Supervisors for their tireless efforts and commitment towards improving cleanliness standards across Delhi. She said, “The most vital part of any Municipality is its sanitation workforce - the Sanitation Inspectors and staff. While a doctor provides medicine after diagnosis, we are the team that works before the doctor. By ensuring cleanliness and sanitation for all, we prevent disease. We are the true givers of health to society, as our Swachhata work reduces illness and enables citizens to lead a healthier, higher quality of life.”
The workshop concluded with a shared commitment from all stakeholders to work collectively towards implementing practical, citizen-centric and results-oriented measures that will contribute to making Delhi cleaner.

Union Minister of Panchayati Raj and Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh called for the participation of all stakeholders in the efforts being made towards achieving ‘Atmanirbhar Panchayats’ (self-reliant Panchayats) and ‘Viksit Panchayats’ (developed Panchayats).
He was addressing the National Workshop on the People’s Plan Campaign (PPC) 2026-27
, organised by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj in New Delhi on 30th October 2026, that saw participation of over 400 participants from across the country. During the workshop,
PPC 2026–27 booklet (
English
/

was also released. Additionally, the
Ministry also signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Convergence Energy Services Limited (CESL)
, a wholly owned subsidiary of Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL) under the Ministry of Power,
for establishing Electric Vehicle (EV) charging and battery swapping stations on Panchayat land
throughout the country.
Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh
informed the gathering about the landmark decision of the Union Cabinet approving the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana (PM VGSY), a next-generation governance transformation initiative aligned with the national vision of Viksit Bharat.
Outlining the key objectives of PM VGSY, the Union Minister highlighted the need to create awareness about government schemes, promote discussions and deliberations at the grassroots level, integrate Centre and State schemes across departments through a common digital platform, ensure timely preparation of Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) and build the capacities of Panchayat representatives and stakeholders for effective grassroots governance.
He said that the approval of PM VGSY reflects the Government’s abiding faith in Panchayats as the foundation of democracy and recognises that the vision of Viksit Bharat can be realised only through Viksit Panchayats. Panchayats, he observed, become truly Atmanirbhar when Gram Sabhas plan with confidence, Own Source Revenue (OSR) is steadily augmented and every level of government works in convergence.
Underlining that Gram Panchayats need to enhance their own-source revenue generation to become eligible for performance grants, he urged them to work towards the Sankalp of ‘Atmanirbhar Panchayat’ for achieving the goal of Viksit Bharat 2047.
The Union Minister urged all stakeholders to work together to strengthen Panchayats and enable them to explore sustainable sources of revenue, ensuring that local development is driven by local priorities. Highlighting that the People’s Plan Campaign (PPC) 2026–27, launched on 2 October 2026, has placed citizens at the centre of the planning process, he emphasised the importance of participatory planning, digital platforms and Jan Bhagidari, as envisioned by Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi.
Dr. Vineet Joshi, Secretary, Ministry of Panchayati Raj,
in his keynote address, said that the Cabinet’s decision on PM VGSY provides a strong foundation for decentralised, evidence-based planning. He highlighted that the
PPC, run by the Ministry since 2018 under the theme “Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas”, has evolved into a robust framework for the preparation of Gram, Block and District Panchayat Development Plans, the localisation of the Sustainable Development Goals, and the convergence of schemes and resources.
Emphasizing upon structured, participatory and inclusive planning, he noted that the Sixteenth Finance Commission, for the award period 2026-31, has recommended total grants amounting to Rs.4,35,236 Crore for duly constituted Panchayati Raj Institutions/ Rural Local Bodies in all 28 States, placing greater responsibility on Gram Panchayats to ensure optimal utilization of funds.
Dr. Joshi stressed that GPDPs should be comprehensive development plans based on people’s needs and aspirations
, rather than being limited to available schemes or funding sources, and underlined the need for an OSR component in GPDPs, as performance-based grants are linked to revenue generation by Panchayats. He called for technology-enabled integration/ convergence of the portals of the Centre and the States, including eGramSwaraj and the Samarth Panchayat Portal, so that integrated data supports better outcome-based planning at the grassroots. Dr. Joshi said that PM VGSY will ensure holistic planning at the Gram Panchayat level, and emphasized upon the need for active participation in Gram Sabhas, use of local data, inter-departmental convergence, improved quality of GPDPs for FY 2027-28, and experience-sharing among the States.
Shri Ashok K. K. Meena, Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation
, said that Panchayats have a central role in ensuring sustained delivery of drinking water and sanitation services, which is directly linked to health and dignity.
He highlighted the significant role of Gram Panchayats in water and waste management, and stressed their training and capacity building through PM VGSY
. He said that GPDPs should adequately address issues of water and sanitation including water sources, quality, maintenance, availability of trained manpower along with garbage management, and underlined the effective utilisation of tied grants under the Sixteenth Finance Commission, with Jal Seva and Swachh Seva Aankalan used to identify gaps and incorporate the findings into GPDPs. Emphasizing upon the broader vision of augmenting the OSR of Panchayats, Shri Meena highlighted the importance of user charges for sustaining water and sanitation services, so that Panchayats progress towards financial self-reliance.
He called for greater accountability of Gram Panchayats through Gram Sabhas, with data used to support better planning, investment and informed decision-making.
Smt. Palka Sahni, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, highlighted the progress made through thematic Panchayat Development Plans and the need to further strengthen their quality, comprehensiveness and responsiveness to local development priorities. Ms. Rohini R. Bhajibhakare, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Rural Development emphasised the need for comprehensive and convergent Gram Panchayat Development Plans to ensure holistic rural development. The Workshop will be followed by State-, District- and Block-level orientations to guide Panchayats in preparing quality, participatory and convergent Development Plans for FY 2027–28.
MoU to Establish Vehicle (EV) Charging and Battery Swapping Stations on Panchayat land
In a significant step towards strengthening the financial sustainability of Panchayats and advancing India’s clean energy agenda, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Convergence Energy Services Limited (CESL), a wholly owned subsidiary of Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL) under the Ministry of Power, for establishing Electric Vehicle (EV) charging and battery swapping stations on Panchayat land. The MoU was signed in the presence of Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, Union Minister of Panchayati Raj, and Shri (Dr.) Vineet Joshi, Secretary, Ministry of Panchayati Raj and was exchanged by Smt. Mukta Shekhar, Joint Secretary, MoPR and Shri Akhilesh Kumar Dixit, Director, CESL. It marks an innovative convergence of rural local governance, green mobility and sustainable revenue generation. The partnership will create new Own Sources of Revenue (OSR) opportunities for Gram, Block and District Panchayats across States and Union Territories, and take clean mobility infrastructure beyond urban centres, including suitable locations along State and National Highways and Panchayat premises, for two-wheelers, three-wheelers, four-wheelers, and medium and heavy-duty vehicles. The Ministry will facilitate coordination with State Panchayati Raj Departments for identification and monitoring of suitable sites, while CESL will undertake site assessment, demand aggregation, supply, installation, testing, commissioning, operation and maintenance.
The initiative is aligned with the Ministry’s efforts to empower Panchayats through enhanced OSR generation, including the recently released Model Panchayat Tax, Rates and Fees Rules (Model OSR Rules), which provide a framework for transparent, accountable and locally driven revenue mobilisation. Panchayat land will become a productive community asset, generating recurring income for civic services, infrastructure and community welfare, while improving access to EV services and reducing carbon emissions in rural areas. Through this collaboration, MoPR and CESL will explore how Panchayat-level public assets can help expand access to electric-mobility infrastructure while contributing to the broader objectives of clean and green villages, sustainable local development and financially stronger Panchayats.

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Department of Atomic Energy and Department of Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh has emphasised nationwide outreach by the Indian Institute of Public Administration (IIPA) as a key priority for ensuring inclusive capacity building in governance.
Stressing the need to move beyond the national capital, he said that expanding IIPA’s geographical reach would help make its learning resources, academic activities and professional networks accessible to a wider community.
Addressing IIPA’s 72nd Annual General Body Meeting, Dr. Jitendra Singh, Chairman of the IIPA Executive Council, spoke in the presence of the Vice President of India and President of IIPA, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, along with senior officials, members of the Institute’s governing bodies and representatives of its academic and administrative community.
Referring to IIPA’s efforts to extend its activities beyond the national capital, the Minister said that this experience had proved motivating. He emphasised the importance of building on this momentum and strengthening the Institute’s presence across the country so that capacity-building opportunities in public administration are not confined to Delhi but reach officials and professionals in different regions.
Dr. Jitendra Singh stressed the need to further strengthen IIPA’s Regional and Local Branches and use them as important channels for wider participation, professional engagement and the dissemination of knowledge. A stronger regional presence would help the Institute connect more effectively with public administration professionals and extend its academic and capacity-building activities to a broader geographical base.
The Minister also referred to the broadening of IIPA’s membership framework, including opportunities for younger professionals and recent graduates to become part of the Institute. With its membership reaching 11,611, IIPA has an opportunity to engage a wider and more diverse community, bringing together experienced administrators, young professionals, researchers and others interested in public administration.
Dr. Jitendra Singh emphasised the role of digital learning and online courses in widening access to knowledge and training. He also stressed the importance of collaboration with the private sector and exploring different ways of making learning resources available to a larger audience. Such efforts can complement the Institute’s physical presence and help expand participation in capacity-building programmes.
Recalling the legacy of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and the role of the civil services in nation-building, the Minister spoke about IIPA’s institutional journey since its establishment in 1954. content:
DoLR Secretary reviews watershed development works in villages of Khed in Pune District under WDC-PMKSY 2.0
Shri Dilip Kumar, Secretary, Department of Land Resources (DoLR), Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, reviewed watershed development works under the Watershed Development Component of Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana 2.0 (WDC-PMKSY 2.0) in Varude, Gulani and Wafgaon villages of Pune district, Maharashtra, on 30 October 2026. The key objectives of watershed development under the scheme include soil and water conservation measures, enhancing agricultural productivity, and promoting sustainable rural development.
Interacting with villagers after inspecting the works, Shri Dilip Kumar said, “
Water is the foundation of our future. Every drop of rain must be conserved to make villages water-secure and self-reliant.
”
He urged villagers to take collective responsibility for regular maintenance and repair of the water harvesting structures created under Watershed Development Scheme, so that these assets remain functional for the next 20 years. He also called for sustained efforts to transform villages under the Khed Project into water-secure and self-reliant communities, on the lines of Hiware Bazar.
Shri Nitin Khade, Joint Secretary (WM), DoLR; Dr. Jitendra Papalkar, Secretary, Soil and Water Conservation Department, Government of Maharashtra, and Smt. Ashwini Jagtap, Deputy Chief Executive Officer, Vasundhara Watershed Development Agency, participated in the visit.
The Secretary visited watershed structures developed using the ridge-to-valley approach, including Continuous Contour Trenches (CCT), earthen nala bunds, cement nala bunds, Kolhapuri-type weirs and ponds for water storage. He reviewed the effectiveness of these structures in reducing rainwater runoff, enhancing groundwater recharge and improving water availability for agriculture, changes in groundwater levels and benefits received by beneficiaries.
The Secretary also reviewed farm ponds, horticulture plantations and agricultural equipment provided to beneficiaries under the scheme, along with benefits extended to women’s self-help groups.
Villagers stated that watershed development works across 11 villages under the Khed Project had improved groundwater levels, enabling farmers to cultivate two to three crops annually thereby increasing agricultural income and rural livelihoods. They added that despite the drought-like conditions this year, water stored in farm ponds and improved water levels in wells associated with cement nala bunds and CCT structures have helped irrigate standing crops.
On 29 October 2026, Secretary DoLR chaired a review meeting at Yashada, Pune with Secretary, Soil and Water Conservation Department, Government of Maharashtra. He also reviewed the status of the WDC-PMKSY scheme, its financial and physical progress.
Shri Dilip Kumar directed officials to prioritise timely completion of water conservation works in drought-prone areas of Maharashtra, with a focus on enhancing water storage capacity and water security. Against the backdrop of El Nino conditions, he emphasised the need to expedite works in the 76 talukas covered under the scheme among the State’s 304 drought-affected talukas. Watershed development works are key to effectively reduce the impact of drought. Priority works include percolation tanks, storage ponds, storage bunds and Kolhapuri-type weirs, which are expected to improve rainwater storage, strengthen village water availability, provide protective irrigation to crops and reduce the vulnerability of agriculture to drought-like conditions.
The meeting emphasised completion of projects within stipulated timelines, maintenance of quality standards, strengthening of Central-State coordination and effective utilisation of available funds.
The visit highlighted that watershed development works are key to effectively reducing the impacts of drought, and reinforced the importance of long-term maintenance of water conservation structures and community participation in building water-secure villages for building a Viksit Bharat.

title: Ministry Of Social Justice And Empowerment Issues Factual Report With Regard To The Claim—Appearing In A Report Published In The Central Chronicle (Bhopal) On October 31, 2026
subtitle: Claim That MAPCET Made Payments Amounting To Crores Based On Placements Without Verifying The Placement Data, Is Entirely Incorrect And Baseless
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 OCT 2026 8:38PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment has issued a factual report with regard to the claim—appearing in a report published in
The Central Chronicle (Bhopal),
on October 31, 2026.
The claim with regard to Madhya Pradesh Council for Employment and Training (MAPCET), having made payments amounting to crores based on placements without verifying the placement data,
is entirely incorrect and baseless.
The factual report is attached herewith, for publishing the same with accuracy and factual context:
FACTUAL REPORT REGARDING THE NEWS ITEM PUBLISHED IN
CENTRAL CHRONICLE, BHOPAL, ON 31 OCTOBER 2026
The Office of the Commissioner, Scheduled Caste Development Department, sanctioned an amount of Rs. 3,241.37 lakh for skill development training under the “Special Central Assistance for Scheduled Caste Sub-Plan” head.
Against this amount,
a total of Rs. 2,945.37 lakh was made available to the Madhya Pradesh Employment and Training Council (MAPCET) during 2021–22. This amount comprised Rs. 1,296.00 lakh (vide Order No. 4695 dated 26 November 2021) and Rs. 1,649.37 lakh
(vide Order No. 10283 dated 25 March 2022).
The Madhya Pradesh Council for Employment and Training (MAPCET) issued a request for proposal (RFP) for the training of beneficiaries from below-poverty-line (BPL) families belonging to the Scheduled Caste (SC) category for the year 2021–22. Following the selection process, contracts were signed with 34 training provider organisations, and work orders were subsequently issued to them. Of these, six organisations did not commence the work.
After the work orders were issued by MAPCET, 28 institutions provided training to 4,952 trainees. The training programmes conducted by the Council comply with the standards prescribed by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India.
All training activities are managed through a dedicated portal, which facilitates trainee registration, daily attendance tracking, and the uploading of assessment and placement data.
Under Clause 2.1.1 of Schedule IV to the Gazette notification issued by the Government of India, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Notification No. 349 dated 4 December 2020, the payment criteria for training providers conducting training in batch mode are as follows:
No.
Instalment

Milestone
1
First
30%

2
Second
40%
Successful completion of certification. Payment is made for the number of candidates certified, after adjustment of advance payments.
3

30%
Achievement of 70% verified employment: continuous employment for three months, with desk verification and placement verification in accordance with standard norms.
The first and second instalments have been paid to the training provider organisations in accordance with the criteria and contractual terms prescribed by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India.
The first instalment is paid when a training batch commences, following physical verification of the trainees. The second instalment is paid after the training has been completed and the trainees have been assessed.
The assessment is conducted by entities designated by the National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET).
Trainees must have attended at least 70 per cent of the training to be eligible for assessment. The first and second instalments have been disbursed on this basis.
The post-training placement information submitted by the training provider institutions in hard-copy form is based on job offers or offer letters. Such submissions do not constitute the basis for releasing the third instalment. To qualify for the third instalment, institutions must upload placement details to the portal in accordance with the prescribed criteria. Only then can the portal generate payment claims for the third instalment. As no such payment claims have been generated for any of these institutions, no third-instalment payments have been made.
The claim made in the news report published in Central Chronicle, Bhopal, on 31 October 2026—that MAPCET disbursed crores of rupees on the basis of placements without verifying the placement data—
is entirely incorrect and baseless.
• The third instalment, which is conditional upon placement, has not been paid to any of the institutions.
Therefore, the question of tracking such placements for the purpose of releasing this instalment does not arise.
• The institutions have received only the first and second instalments, neither of which is linked to placement.
Accordingly, placement or placement tracking is not relevant to the payments already made.
The third instalment will be paid when candidates take up employment after completing their training.
The organisation is currently facilitating placements.
